brief: In early September Citadel Securities strategist Scott Rubner told clients to reduce exposure and buy cheap protection, calling it a tactical downside window, then mid-month warned September weakness might not be finished. With September over and the hedges having worked, his note "October: The Q4 Reload" turns bullish into Q4: positioning and leverage fell, retail cooled, systematic (CTA) flows sold, and valuations compressed, so earnings season, reopening buyback windows and below-neutral CTA positioning now have room to push stocks higher. He separately flags that the S&P's gain masks the worst market breadth since the dot-com bust, with four mega-caps driving most of Q3's index gain while the average stock and cyclicals (per Goldman's industrials desk) lagged, and single-stock dispersion/vol have cooled from summer extremes. He expects not a straight line higher but October volatility offering a better entry, and says he would use early-Q4 weakness to add to core longs, preferring single names. Midterm-year seasonality (Q4 average +5.6% vs 2.9% overall) supports the call, though Q4 lows have historically formed in October 58% of the time.
